protocol:
1. Arrange the work area with a green ice bucket containing labeled microcentrifuge tubes on ice, a yellow PCR tube rack, disposable pipette tips in a blue tip box, and an adjustable single-channel pipette.

2. Pick up an open thin-walled PCR tube with a gloved hand and hold it near the pipette tip for liquid addition.

3. Attach a disposable pipette tip to the single-channel pipette from the tip box.

4. Dispense liquid sample or reagent from the pipette into the open PCR tube while holding the tube by hand.

5. Place the filled PCR tube upright into the yellow PCR tube rack.

6. Repeat the transfer workflow for additional PCR tubes, using the pipette and disposable tips to add liquid sample or reagent to each tube.

7. Keep labeled microcentrifuge tubes in the green ice bucket between transfers to maintain the samples or reagents cold.

8. Remove a labeled microcentrifuge tube from the ice bucket and hold it open for pipetting.

9. Pipette liquid sample or reagent into or out of the opened microcentrifuge tube using the single-channel pipette.

10. Return the microcentrifuge tube to the ice bucket after the transfer.

11. Place the prepared PCR tube into the yellow rack and continue assembling the remaining PCR tubes.

12. Set the pipette down on the bench and close the prepared PCR tube by pressing the cap shut with gloved hands.

13. Carry the closed PCR tube from the bench to the Bio-Rad T100 Thermal Cycler.

14. Open the heated lid of the Bio-Rad T100 Thermal Cycler and load the prepared PCR tube into the thermal cycler block.

15. Close the heated lid of the Bio-Rad T100 Thermal Cycler.

16. Select the saved protocol menu on the Bio-Rad T100 Thermal Cycler touchscreen.

17. Select the saved protocol named “PHANTA” from the protocol list.

18. Start the “PHANTA” thermal cycling program with a displayed reaction volume setting of 20 µL and a lid temperature of 105°C.

19. Run the displayed thermal cycling program with steps shown on the screen: 95°C for 3:00, then a cycling segment including 95°C for 0:10, 67°C for 0:05, and 72°C for 0:30, followed by 72°C for 1:00 and a 12°C hold.

20. Monitor the Bio-Rad T100 status screen after starting the run; the screen displays the sample temperature, lid heating status, and remaining run time.
